notes: Condensed from the 0.4.1 session-ownership work. Security reasoning, a rejected alternative, and a deliberate 404-over-403 choice.

messages.content: Any caller can read any session. Close it.
Confirmed the IDOR: every session-scoped route takes session_id from the URL and there is one shared deployment key, so nothing ties a session to a caller.
Worse — clients choose their own session_id in the request body, so no guessing is needed. Decided: bind each session to the credential that first used it.
how do you tell callers apart with one key
Decided: an api_keys list where each credential is its own principal. Created security/ownership.py with an OwnershipStore backed by SQLite.

Decided: 404 rather than 403. A distinguishable 403 turns the routes into an oracle for which session names exist. Completed: verify_session_access in routes_graph.py, wired into all 15 session routes.
No. With no key configured every caller is one principal, so local single-user use is unchanged. Completed: the ownership tests, and all 446 tests pass.

completed_tasks: security/ownership.py with an OwnershipStore backed by SQLite
decisions: bind each session to the credential
